What's the difference between cached and uncached?

Cached is served from CloudFlare servers. It means it's "saved" on CloudFlare server and just served from there to relieve the pressure on Voat. Uncached means actually live from Voat.

This is a feature that CloudFlare provides to its users (Voat is a user) along with DDoS protection (checking if you are a bot and throttling/blocking you).
Ok, so it's only understandable cached bandwidth would go up when it's doing the checking your bits thing AKA DDOS attack?
Yes. Generally cached content is what users not logged in see, thumbnails, CSS, the ad and logo. uncached content is freshly created for you.

Well, that page is small in size. Maybe if it's a bot spamming Voat and getting that page millions of times then it will increase the count of cached served go up.

Generally cache is used for things like images, CSS (page style), JS (code that runs like for submitting a comment). That's because these things generally shouldn't change (unless Voat is rolling a new release). The main thing that shouldn't be normally cached is actual HTML content like my comment because there can always be new comments/votes/etc.

Some more info here:

https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200168256-What-are-CloudFlare-s-caching-levels-

https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200172516-Which-file-extensions-does-CloudFlare-cache-for-static-content

along with DDoS protection (checking if you are a bot and throttling/blocking you).
